Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and attached a redlined version (MediSys_DPA_Redlines_20250301.pdf). A few points to confirm quickly:

- We need a current list of subprocessors and whether any process EEA customer data outside the EU. Please provide a CSV with vendor name, purpose, and hosting region.
- Audit rights: MediSys typically requires on-site/third-party audit rights and a 30-day notice. If you cannot accommodate on-site audits, can you provide SOC 2 Type II report and a recent pen test executive summary?
- Data transfers: for EEA data we prefer SCCs or an equivalent (please confirm Redwood's approach).

Can you route the redlines to your legal team and let us know your position? We prefer to sign via DocuSign once legal is aligned.

Attachments: MediSys_DPA_Redlines_20250301.pdf

Thanks,

Emma —

Appreciate the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Markus (legal) and Dev (SE) to handle the legal/technical details. Quick answers while they look:

- Subprocessors: I'll share our current list (Subprocessor_List_2025.csv). We host customer inference workloads in AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), GCP (us-central1) and in our EU region (europe-west1). Some infra vendors are US-based — we'll mark locations in the CSV.
- Audit rights: Redwood's standard position is to provide SOC 2 Type II report and an independent penetration test summary in lieu of unlimited on-site audits. We'll attach those reports if that's acceptable.
- Data transfers: We use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers from the EEA and can append any customer-specific addendum where required.

Markus — can you take the redlines and propose language we can send back? Emma, can you indicate which specific clauses around audit and remedies are non-negotiable for MediSys? That will help Markus prioritize.

Next step: Markus will return a counter and then we can aim to finalize for DocuSign by early next week.

Subject: Redwood DPA counter & proposed audit/subprocessor language

Emma —

Thanks for sending your redlines. I've reviewed MediSys's requests and attached our counterparty doc (Redwood_DPA_Counter_v2.docx) with specific edits. Highlights below so we can stay aligned:

1) Subprocessors
- We will provide a current subprocessor list (attached Subprocessor_List_2025.csv) and notify customers 30 days before adding a subprocessor that will process production data.
- We cannot accept an open-ended approval right over subprocessors; we propose a limited approval clause: Customer may object within 15 business days to a new subprocessor on reasonable security grounds, and Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to address the objection (including offering alternative controls).

2) Audit Rights
- Redwood's standard approach: provide SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and an executive summary of the latest third-party penetration test.
- For customers requiring additional assurance, we offer a scoped, third-party assessment by an independent auditor under mutual NDA. We cannot commit to unrestricted on-site audits.
- Proposed clause (suggestion included in the attached doc): "Customer may request evidence of Redwood's security program (SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary). If Customer requires additional assessment, parties will agree on scope, timing, and cost allocation for a mutually agreed third-party auditor."

3) Data Transfers
- We will execute SCCs for EEA transfers and will include our standard data transfer addendum. If MediSys requires a specific addendum (e.g., Swiss addendum), please indicate and we'll review.

I've tried to be constructive and accommodate MediSys's need for assurance while keeping our processes predictable for all customers. If those positions look OK, I'm happy to accept your non-substantive edits and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Counter_v2.docx; Subprocessor_List_2025.csv; SOC2-TypeII-summary-2024.pdf; PenTest-Executive-Summary-2024.pdf

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Jordan / Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. MediSys legal reviewed Redwood's counter and the SOC2/pen test summaries. We made only one non-substantive edit to the signature block and are ready to execute. Please send a DocuSign envelope for the DPA and the SOW. I attached a copy for our records (MediSys_DPA_Accepted_20250305.pdf).

Can you confirm Redwood will notify us 30 days in advance of any subprocessor changes to the list you sent? Also confirm that Redwood will execute the SCCs for EEA customer data.
